prompt: A brutally simple physics diagram illustrating two objects in motion. Two identical circles (representing spheres) are drawn side-by-side with generous horizontal spacing. The left circle contains the label X centered inside it. The right circle contains the label Y centered inside it. From the right edge of each circle, a simple straight horizontal arrow points to the right to indicate motion. The arrows should be the same length. The image is illustrative only and not answer-bearing. Style: professional monochrome admissions-test diagram. Use clean black vector-like strokes on a pure white #FFFFFF background. The labels X and Y must be in a Times New Roman-like serif font. No other labels, no extra arrows, no shading, no 3D rendering, and no background clutter.
negative_prompt: Pure white background only; no grey paper, gradient, or texture. No extra labels. No overlap. No sans-serif fonts. No decorative shading. No photorealism. No colour. No exact answer-bearing measurements. No clutter. No malformed symbols. Do not place objects in the wrong support/location relationship. No unrequested arrows, force labels, field symbols, construction arcs, or explanatory overlays.

must_show_relations: Circles must be side-by-side and clearly separated
Each circle must have exactly one horizontal arrow pointing right
relative_size_constraints: Both circles should appear roughly the same size
Both arrows should appear roughly the same length

hard_constraints: Labels X and Y must be centered inside their respective circles
Background must be pure white #FFFFFF with no grey fill or gradient
No unrequested arrows, force labels, field symbols, or construction arcs
